# T79 Unify Qt and Pygame match presentation after T66

- **Implementer**: native Codex **Sol Medium**, owner batch authorization2026-10-18; retains choice through rework.
- **Reviewer**: owner-selected **MiniMax M3** after validated PR; main launches independent review.
- **Evidence**: [confirmed: original kit424d599/F014 and T65 accepted worker bridge; designed: owner #182, T66 and system.md] T66 must merge first; its accepted API and paths are required at dispatch. See [audit](../design/football-gui/audit.md) for exact pins and [system](../design/football-gui/system.md) for proposal tokens.
- **Owns**: `goal2/desktop/pygame_viewer.py`; new Qt presentation helper `match_page.py`; `fixtures_page.py` (delegate existing play/halftime construction without changing T78 cards); `window.py` (minimal presentation calls only); `tools/desktop-ui/redesign.py` (match-handoff dispatch), new `match_handoff_scenario.py`; `goal2/tests/test_pygame_match_view.py` and `goal2/tests/test_pygame_pitch_view.py` (replace obsolete presentation pixel expectations with new substantive rendering/read-only/layout oracles, preserving lifecycle assertions); `docs/desktop-management.md` and `docs/design/football-gui/system.md` when made inaccurate; `docs/evidence/T79/**`.
- **Scope**: [designed] Apply shared colors, typography intent, scoreboard/provenance and readable original-commentary/result boards to the accepted T66/T83 presentation seam. Style busy/progress/cancel and existing quick halftime decisions coherently. This protects read-only viewer packets, responsive Qt and once-only publication. Preserve the accepted animated pitch, numbered markers, frame consumption and pacing/publication contract; apply style only. No new IPC protocol, engine adapter, competitive watching, new pitch animation, in-play edits or mid-match save.
- **Done when** (proposed command contracts; main must establish fail-before/mock-positive preflight before dispatch, using verified local resources):
  1. [designed] `python3 tools/desktop-ui/redesign.py --scenario match-handoff --template <verified-template> --data <verified-GOAL.DAT> --evidence-dir docs/evidence/T79/linux` passes: Run real Qt/SDL events for non-default-country original friendly through progress, result, Save/Resume and repeat; compare ordered displayed values and complete state with direct original output. Verify heartbeat while blocked, duplicate/stale packets, viewer close/failure/repeated cancel, both-window shutdown and save-byte retention; retain T66 bounded reaping checks. Capture Qt+Pygame windows/focus at required sizes/scaling.
  2. [designed] Run the same scenario on real Windows Qt (and SDL where applicable),100%/200% scaling; retain new repo-owned screenshots, interaction report, exact OS/Qt versions and source-resource hashes under `docs/evidence/T79/windows`. No original screenshots/assets or personal save files enter git. Linux offscreen alone cannot accept this line.
  3. [designed] `python3 -m unittest goal2.tests.test_pygame_match_view goal2.tests.test_desktop_quick_jobs -v` and applicable existing desktop acceptance/proof commands pass; `python3 tools/check_premerge.py --expected-head <reviewed-sha>` passes on clean exact head. Record a behavioral negative control: Let rendering mutate a packet/state, block the Qt heartbeat, start two jobs or publish on full_time before the tail: the accepted T66 lifecycle checks plus the new handoff scenario must fail. Baseline lacks unified presentation.
- **Hazards**: [designed] Ordinarily merge accepted main; preserve T66 window.py changes and read its actual module paths. Transitions never run engines. Keep optional-dependency errors actionable; preserve Qt ownership, process limits and original-output labels.

[designed: main preflight clarification, 2026-10-18] Actual merged T66/T83 viewer and lifecycle APIs are the baseline; reuse accepted `style.COLORS` including contrast-corrected divider, preserve animated pitch/project geometry, markers, frame consumption and publication/pacing. Historical stage1/no-animation wording must be attributed historically. Genuine country18 Malta starts as source B versus country32 and supplies IDs341–351. Retained lifecycle/engine/provenance/premerge gates already pass baseline; new presentation/read-only assertions must fail before and pass a planning mock. Qt actual ratio and SDL actual driver/window/surface pixel sizes/font metrics/Windows DPI are separate measurements: QT_SCALE_FACTOR alone cannot prove SDL scaling. Main must establish actual Windows SDL dependency and substantive native mock evidence, then publish concrete scale/capture constraints before implementation GO. The source freeze, raw failure corrections and complete-packet ACK/observer ownership distinction are retained under `docs/evidence/T79/main-preflight-02`.

[designed: main scope clarification, 2026-10-18; confirmed: main-preflight-02/pitch-presentation-planning.log] Shared-palette styling necessarily changes three retained pitch-test pixel expectations (background, score text/background/position and country-label background). Main proved all three pass accepted baseline and fail the runtime palette mock at those assertions. Updating those presentation expectations in test_pygame_pitch_view.py is authorized; preserve every independent signed-axis, marker/ball, visibility, watermark, queue, cadence, flip-before-consumption, pacing and ACK assertion. No new pitch animation or lifecycle change is authorized. [confirmed: main native preflight, docs/evidence/T79/main-preflight-03/audit.json] Main completed and audited all12 native Windows baseline/mock/negative jobs on frozen ccc659fc, with four protected original files unchanged. Qt ratios1/2 and SDL driver/window/surface/font/DPI are measured separately. Actual SDL original matches remain1000×720/DPI96; compact/larger synthetic surfaces demonstrate feasibility only. Do not fix scrolling by enabling all management controls. Preserve intentional match-busy editing guards; if allowing busy inspection, prove it independently and do not mutate jobs.
- Test active and preview countries independently, both tables, first/last/full-ID selected-player detail. Use genuine input dispatch, acquire/assert focus, and prove row/scroll visibility after input, not a programmatic scroll-to-only test. Check all20/80-row reading coverage at actual1x1440x900,1050x780,900x700 and2x900x640. Main runs Windows final frozen-source acceptance.

[designed: owner playtest, 2026-10-19] The newer Windows build makes it hard to find how to play a match. Starting a watched match offers no way to slow playback.

[confirmed: accepted source b6634227] `ManagementWindow.start_watched()` calls `self.watched.start()` without exposing a rate. `WatchedController.start(playback_rate=...)` already accepts 1–240 samples/s; default is60. This task exposes existing presentation pacing, not new engine timing or game rules.

Scope: provide an obvious primary Play/Watch route from the startup/overview screen; distinguish quick results from watching the animated pitch; explain real prerequisites/refusals adjacent to the action. Provide a clearly labeled pre-match Slow/Normal/Fast selector, with a retained slower choice and Normal preserving the existing60-samples/s default. Freeze the chosen rate per running match; lock speed editing while busy. Use the existing playback_rate argument without changing engine stepping, RNG, packet/queue/ACK/publication protocols, result or save schemas. Do not invent unsupported watched modes or silently bypass unconfirmed drafts.

Done when:
- Real keyboard/mouse actions from a newly opened game reach the intended match route, with clear confirmation/missing-runtime/unsupported-fixture guidance and reachable controls at accepted Windows1x/2x sizes.
- Selecting Slow before Watch passes the exact supported slower rate into the real controller/viewer; Normal remains60; a measured sample/elapsed-time observation demonstrates slower playback without merely slowing the engine.
- Different presentation rates give identical complete original output/state/seeds/events/results; all frames remain ordered, acknowledged after painting, and publication waits for consumed tail. Existing cancel/busy/duplicate/stale/owned-child/save-retention checks still hold.
- Choice remains stable across redraw/navigation and is read afresh for each explicitly started match; no accidental auto-start or mutable in-flight rate. Define persistence scope before implementation; no save-schema extension.
- Meaningful fail-before/pass-after and wrong-rate/ignored-selection controls, applicable retained match/overview checks and exact-head premerge pass. Main executes actual Windows frozen-source gate; MiniMax reviews independently.

Owner selected Native Sol Low implementation and MiniMax M3 review. Coordinate with active T79/PR240 so the new match presentation is retained. Planning/contract first; implementation has not begun. Preserve both launchers, all Windows saves and every worktree.

issues.body:
[designed: issue #244 manual audit] Give a manager direct, readable control of the original decision set that the current Squad & tactics desktop does not expose: a selected player's position/club-role choice, individual possession/passing/tackling choices, opponent marking, and a comprehensible formation summary. The original showed these beside the player card; M244-G1A-02 steps 3–11 and E031 C31–C33 provide observed navigation and field labels. See the illustrated [manual chapter](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2/blob/docs/244-original-game-manual/docs/original-game/squad-and-tactics.md) and [audit](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2/blob/docs/244-original-game-manual/docs/original-game/remaster-audit.md).

Current `goal2/desktop/squad_page.py` presents XI, captain and eight team-tactic checkboxes; its selected-player detail is read-only and contains no personal-tactic or position editor. #242 separately owns *display* of complete attributes and personal-tactic values, and #241 owns scrolling. This request must coordinate with both rather than duplicate their controls or claims.

Proposed bounded scope: first map each verified choice to existing state/engine support and list unsupported choices; then add a draft-safe editing route only for supported choices. Show current selection, proposed change and opponent/mark context; preserve full player identity, preview read-only behavior, explicit Confirm/Discard, and small-window keyboard/mouse access. Do not invent a formation algorithm, modify original engine rules, or silently turn an unsupported mark into a no-op. Acceptance should show a real before/after management decision surviving save/resume or clearly refuse unsupported options without changing state.

Issue #244 is the reference; implementation ownership/priority/review are for main-session triage. [confirmed: M244-G1A-02; E031 C31–C33; current desktop code; designed: proposed UI]

The desktop has no comparable browsable whole-round fixture/opponent view, country history or bulletin. Existing T50–T59 separately own campaign rules/progression; this is an information/navigation slice, not authority to implement absent draws or match-watch flags.

Proposed bounded scope: inventory data already held in the current model and distinguish absent data; present verified available next/previous fixture, sides, type, group positions and adjacent results together, with readable empty/unsupported states. Make Overview lead to it with an obvious action. Defer original-style watch toggles, news events, rankings or career records unless their source and persistence are established. Acceptance should exercise actual keyboard/mouse navigation and small-window scrolling, show correct country/fixture context after a result and Resume, and preserve game/save state while browsing.

Issue #244 is the original-game reference; implementation priority and owner await main-session triage. [confirmed: M244-G1A-03; E031 C17–C20; desktop code; designed: proposed UI]

The [match manual](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2/blob/docs/244-original-game-manual/docs/original-game/match-and-results.md) separates observed E031 C38–C50 branches from still-missing screenshot states.

Current `goal2/desktop/pygame_viewer.py` is read-only presentation; `window.py` locks management during Watch. The quick-friendly worker has a separate Qt halftime substitution path. T79/#198 owns match *presentation* and explicitly excludes in-play edits, so this must be a later contract rather than a change to its active worktree.

First bounded step: audit which prompts/actions the accepted original watched kit and worker can actually pause for and resume without changing results, RNG, frame order or publication; retain a support matrix with original single-step evidence. Design explicit pause/action/refusal messages only for supported cases. Do not promise competitive watching, a replay viewer, or a substitution rule that the current runtime cannot satisfy. Acceptance for any supported first intervention must use a real original fixture, compare complete continuation/output before and after the choice, and prove cancellation/save safety plus keyboard/mouse focus at small-window sizes.

Issue #244 supplies the illustrated reference; main session owns implementation scope and review dispatch. [confirmed: E031 C38–C50; desktop viewer/window; #198 contract; designed: proposed route]

issues.body:
[designed: issue #244 manual audit] Make past match outcomes discoverable. The original hub offered F4 saved match summaries and F3 saved-goal replays, with comparison statistics after a watched game; see the [start/save/replay](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2/blob/docs/244-original-game-manual/docs/original-game/startup-save-replay.md) and [match/result](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2/blob/docs/244-original-game-manual/docs/original-game/match-and-results.md) chapters (E031 C23–C24b, C51; E015-r0007 states 51 and 207).

Current `goal2/desktop/fixtures_page.py` presents the latest score, result stages and details; `pygame_viewer.py` shows the watched result board while open. There is no user-facing browseable match-summary archive or saved-goal replay library. Historical data retention and playback inputs must be audited first: do not claim a replay exists merely because the original showed one.

Proposed first slice: a read-only list/detail route over match history actually retained by the current save/model, with opponent/date/competition, score, result stages and verified available statistics/scorers. Distinguish unavailable historical fields. Preserve source A/B order, watched-versus-quick provenance, save compatibility and state purity. Scope saved-goal playback separately only after durable event/position evidence exists. Acceptance should browse more than one result after Resume using keyboard/mouse at small window sizes and prove no game or save mutation.

Issue #244 is the reference; main session triages implementation and review. [confirmed: E031 C23–C24b/C51; desktop code; designed: proposed UI]

[confirmed: [MiniMax M3 independent approval](https://github.com/diegoami/goal2/pull/245#issuecomment-6263502453)] PR245 merged as84af745c6b2d68b89077e9fde330fc8538eda031 after native Windows1x/2x, anchored audit, independent21group replay and main accepted-head checks. The review supplied these two nonblocking observations verbatim:

````text
R1 (non-blocking, follow-up): tools/desktop-ui/player-browsing.py lines 50-52 load ManagementWindow and assert `report['ratio']==float(os.environ.get('QT_SCALE_FACTOR','1'))`. On the audited Windows native reports this assertion succeeded because the platform helper honored QT_SCALE_FACTOR=1/2, but the helper has no fall-back if the OS reports a different ratio (e.g., Windows per-monitor DPI on a non-primary screen). The current Windows IT13 runs report qt_ratio == requested scale, so this is not a live defect; it would be cleaner to log a warning rather than fail outright when the OS reports a different DPI than the requested scale. Rate: low likelihood it triggers in current environments.

R2 (non-blocking, follow-up): tools/desktop-ui/player-browsing.py lines 109 sizes = `[(900,640)] if float(os.environ.get('QT_SCALE_FACTOR','1'))==2 else [(1440,900),(1050,780),(900,700)]` compares against the scale factor float rather than the actual device ratio. The earlier `report['ratio']` assertion catches divergence in practice, so this is fine today; a more direct mapping (compare against `report['ratio']`) would make the intent clearer. Rate: low likelihood.
````
